milestone: Brownie Runtime Release Readiness P0/P1 Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Keeps Runtime release readiness tied to executable local Runtime debt classification before new autonomous feature work proceeds.
Preserves the boundary that Runtime-owned permission, tool, cancellation, replay, recovery, and completion debt cannot be hidden inside external platform work.
Keeps workspace mutation and controlled tool release blockers separate from forge, notification, hosted scheduler, and commercial product readiness.

answers.new_capability: Brownie now has a machine-checked Runtime Release Readiness audit that classifies P0/P1 Runtime blockers, owner decisions, out-of-runtime work, and the still-open CI Release Gate before implementation phases begin.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: The prior manifest separated Runtime DoD from external responsibilities, but it did not provide a guarded P0/P1 release-debt inventory or verify that the Runtime release readiness guard remains on the existing CI-invoked VSIX check path.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie could either claim Runtime Release Ready with open Runtime blockers or incorrectly block Runtime release on scheduler, daemon, enterprise, adapter, BDK, or hosted platform work.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase adds a new audit artifact, guard, negative tests, CI wiring, and manifest alignment rather than another readiness summary.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase introduces no protocol method, CLI command, runtime endpoint, or VSIX command.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The audit is a release gate artifact consumed by a guard, not a new runtime inspection, digest, history, verdict, or user-facing summary API.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Release readiness validation now fails closed when open Runtime P0/P1 blockers are misclassified, when out-of-runtime work blocks release, when OSS owner decisions are omitted, or when the existing CI-invoked VSIX check path omits the Runtime release readiness guard.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: The autonomous controller can proceed through finite corrective phases using a guarded list of Runtime-owned blockers instead of drifting into platform or commercial work.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the first required campaign step, Runtime Release debt reaudit, and makes later P0/P1 closure phases auditable.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRD-1 adds a Runtime Release Readiness guard and connects it to CI, so strict review must ensure the new guard cannot mask open Runtime P0/P1 blockers or convert external platform work into release-blocking Runtime debt.

exit_criteria: A human-readable Runtime Release Readiness audit table classifies requested P0/P1/P2 items as implemented sufficient, implemented contract gap, partial, runtime-outside, or owner-decision waiting.
A machine-readable Runtime Release Readiness audit artifact records Runtime Release Ready as false and lists required-before-release Runtime blockers.

A guard rejects missing required Runtime blockers, open Runtime P0/P1 debt that is not required_before_release, out-of-runtime work that blocks Runtime release, missing OSS owner decision while Cargo remains UNLICENSED/publish=false, and missing existing CI-invoked VSIX release guard coverage.
The Runtime release readiness guard is wired into the VSIX check path invoked by existing CI, while full CI Release Gate hardening remains an explicit P0 blocker.
Phase value and Product Completion guards pass without claiming full Runtime Release Ready.
behavior_evidence: node --test scripts/guard-runtime-release-readiness.test.mjs proves valid audit acceptance plus rejection of premature release-ready claim, Runtime P0 misclassification, external release blockers, missing owner license decision, and CI omissions.
pnpm guard:runtime-release-readiness proves the repository audit, Cargo license/publish state, and CI gate are aligned.
pnpm guard:phase-value proves guard-engine changes are represented in this manifest.
pnpm guard:product-completion proves this bounded phase remains a blocker-removal gate and does not claim total Product Completion.

runtime_release_dod: Durable task/run/journey state, checkpoint, ledger, idempotency, stale rejection, replay, conflict, cancellation safety, schema migration, recovery, protocol/event ownership, completion, and finalization.
Agent loop execution, Mode Pack validation/pinning/materialization, permissions, controlled tools, workspace proposal/apply, approvals, and bounded refusal/blocker machinery.
Run Request, Runtime Event, Control Command, and Run Result/Attestation contracts.
commercial_solution_readiness: BDK, Enterprise, Assurance, scheduler, daemon, job queue, worker fleet, Docker/VM/Kubernetes management, tenant management, SSO/RBAC server, admin/approval UI, forge apps, notifications, monitoring backend/dashboard/alert/SLA/billing, private registry, certified stack, and continuity assurance.
does_not_close: Full CI Release Gate workflow hardening

technical_debt.evidence: Boundary contracts exist but need a canonical public protocol contract and compatibility matrix.
Cancelled state exists but explicit caller-authorized cancellation semantics are still partial.
Recovery probe exists but production-equivalent installed process-loss E2E remains open.
Payload schema versions exist but release-level durable store schema and migration behavior remains open.
Existing CI invokes the VSIX check path with the new release readiness guard, but frozen install and direct release guard-test workflow enforcement remain open.
Rust protocol, runtime handlers, store/events, CLI, VSIX, and docs need a guarded ownership map.
M64.15 left Runtime module decomposition open.
Local Runtime deadline, platform, and durability hardening remains open.
Hosted scheduling and worker infrastructure is outside Brownie Runtime release.
Forge and notification workflows are external adapters.
Enterprise, Assurance, BDK, certified stack, continuity assurance, and commercial operations readiness are outside this Runtime campaign.

safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains authority for execution, admission, replay, permission, tool execution, workspace mutation, completion, and finalization.
